style.vernacular: Valley city of layered eras: Ottoman Baščaršija with low whitewashed and stone shops, timber-framed upper storeys and domed stone halls; Austro-Hungarian centre of ochre, cream and pink rendered blocks in Secession and Moorish Revival dress; socialist-era concrete and render housing blocks in Novi Grad and Dobrinja; hillside houses stepping up the slopes under red-orange clay-tile hip roofs; new glass towers (Sead Gološ designs) in Marijin Dvor.
style.ornament: Ottoman: overhanging timber upper storeys, wooden eaves, stone domes and lead roofs, pseudo-Ottoman Sebilj fountain, minarets; Austro-Hungarian: Secession and Moorish Revival friezes, banded stone, cornices; socialist era: bare concrete and render blocks, bullet-scarred walls with red-resin Sarajevo Roses.

sources.what: city architecture: Ottoman Baščaršija core, Austro-Hungarian centre (Secession, Moorish Revival), socialist blocks in Novi Grad, hillside houses
